headline: High: shared-bus Pipecat can feed untrusted content into a shell-capable RAG writer, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a uses a shared bus and stdin/stdout, while agent_b reads/writes files and runs shell/subprocesses. That creates a plausible bridge where Pipecat outputs can be consumed as instructions by the content-writing agent. The pair lacks provenance tracking or isolation in the profiles, so the interaction exists in default-ish setups, though not proven directly.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a stdout or files as prompt text, injection is possible.
IF both agents share the same bus or workspace, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct buses/workspaces.
Add strict provenance tags to all agent_a outputs.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files/stdout.
Review any shared parser for instruction-like content.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, and can call external APIs; agent_b handles configuration secrets and writes files while also using allowlisted network egress. If agent_a outputs land in agent_b's workspace, sensitive conversational or media data can be copied into a secret-bearing environment and then transmitted. The profiles do not show hard isolation, so leakage is plausible in default configurations.
conditions: IF agent_a writes transcripts or media into a shared workspace, agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b forwards workspace contents to allowlisted APIs, copied data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions.
Keep secrets in a vault, not in the shared workspace.
Block agent_b from reading agent_a output folders.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports shared-state multi-instance operation on a shared bus, and agent_b can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. Even though agent_b cannot modify git state, both can mutate overlapping local resources if co-located. The profiles do not document locking or coordination, so write conflicts are plausible and could corrupt outputs or configs.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF agent_a instances share state with agent_b-managed jobs, race conditions can corrupt artifacts.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Make agent_b run read-only for agent_a outputs.
requires-engineering: add transactional state management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate conversational content and agent_b exposes ask/agentic-ask endpoints plus a LangGraph subagent model, so A's output can plausibly become B's input. The profiles do not show a verification gate before B acts, and B also has shell and filesystem authority. That makes downstream amplification likely enough to rate medium, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative context, errors can cascade.
IF agent_b triggers actions from unverified agent_a text, downstream mistakes can be executed.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions.
Require citations or structured outputs from agent_a.
Add a verification pass in agent_b.
Limit agent_b to read-only mode for agent_a outputs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based action gating.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles configuration secrets and requests Docker Desktop plus Airflow credentials, while agent_a is an audio-speech system that can process conversation state and media. If the pair is used on regulated or sensitive content, the mismatch in handling and retention expectations can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not document matching certifications or residency controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through both agents, retention and access controls must align.
IF agent_b logs secrets or transcripts longer than agent_a's policy, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Confirm both agents' retention settings.
Exclude secrets from agent_a transcripts.
Document data residency for each API call.
Restrict regulated data to one agent only.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging.
